To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a structural similarity metric outperforms the state of the art in terms of correlation with human judgment, that this performance is robust to changes in viewing conditions and image resolution, and that the metric has a simple intuitive interpretation.

the structural similarity of two images is a better predictor of perceived image quality than the similarity of the pixel values, and that the proposed structural similarity index can be used for a variety of applications including perceptual image quality prediction, image search, compression, and denoising.

(i) the human visual system is adapted for extracting structural (or pattern) information from a scene; (ii) the degradation of structural similarity between a reference image and a test image is a good predictor of perceived image distortion; (iii) a new image quality metric, called structural similarity, can be derived from this concept and is shown to be a good predictor of human perception; (iv) this structural similarity metric is a simple and intuitive alternative to existing methods for image quality assessment; and
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new objective image quality assessment method based on structural similarity, and its evaluation using both subjective and objective methods.
the development of a perceptually motivated objective image quality metric.
image quality assessment and the design of objective image quality measures.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel framework for quality assessment that is based on the degradation in structural information, and have shown its promise through a number of intuitive examples, comparison to both subjective data and state of the-art methods, and analysis of the behavior of the proposed method.

we have developed a new objective method for image quality assessment that is based on structural information and that outperforms existing methods on a variety of images compressed with both JPEG and JPEG2002.
the structural similarity index is a new perceptual distance metric that can be used for objective image quality assessment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given distortion, the amount of distortion in the image is not the only important factor.
the structural content of an image is a useful feature in image quality assessment.
structural similarity is an important aspect of perceptual image quality, and can be used to complement existing error visibility-based quality assessment methods.
